title: The adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ on module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $j\colon U\to X$ an open immersion.
The extension by zero $j_!$ of [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] is left adjoint to
the pullback $j^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$
of [def-sfb-module-upper-star], by the adjunction obtained by composing
$\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}\dashv\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_j}$
([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]) with
$j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\dashv\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$
([def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek]), and identifying
$\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_j}\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}$.

proof.text: Work in $\mathcal C=\Sh(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, with $\mathcal R=j^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_X$ and $\mathcal S=\Lambda_U$. The tensor structure and the applicability to $\Ab$ and the essentially small pro-étale site are those of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], this category is abelian, symmetric monoidal closed, and tensoring on either side preserves colimits. In particular it has equalizers and coequalizers: in an abelian category these are the kernel and cokernel of the difference of two parallel maps. The coefficient rings here are commutative. Thus parts 3 and 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] apply. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], applied to $f=j$ and the given condensed ring, $\alpha_j:\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ is invertible. Fix the natural isomorphism $\tau:\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}$ supplied by part 5 of change of scalars, in the direction inverse to its displayed isomorphism.

proof.text:
Write $L=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!$, $T=\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$, $A=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}$ and $B=\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_j}$. We have $L\dashv T$ by [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek] and $A\dashv B$ by part 3 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] consequently has left adjoint $L\circ A=j_!$, the equality being the definition in [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], and right adjoint $B\circ T$. Explicitly, for $M\in\Mod_{\Lambda_U}$ and $N\in\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, its Hom bijection is
$$
\Hom_{\Lambda_X}(j_!M,N)=\Hom_{\Lambda_X}(L(AM),N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom_{\mathcal R}(AM,TN)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom_{\Lambda_U}(M,B(TN)).
$$
Both bijections are natural in $M,N$, being the Hom bijections of the stated adjunctions. The domains match because $AM$ and $TN$ are both $\mathcal R$-modules on $U$.

proof.text:
Postcompose the last Hom set in step 2 with $\tau_{TN}$ from step 1. This gives the bijection
$$
\Hom_{\Lambda_X}(j_!M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom_{\Lambda_U}(M,\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}(TN))=\Hom_{\Lambda_U}(M,j^*N),
$$
where the final equality is exactly [def-sfb-module-upper-star] for $f=j$. On that last Hom set the added map is $h\mapsto\tau_{TN}\circ h$, with inverse $h\mapsto\tau_{TN}^{-1}\circ h$. It commutes with precomposition in $M$ by associativity; for a map $v:N\to N'$, naturality in $N$ is the equation $\tau_{TN'}\circ B(Tv)=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}(Tv)\circ\tau_{TN}$, the naturality equation for $\tau$. Hence the resulting bijection is natural in both variables and defines $j_!\dashv j^*$. This defines precisely the composite adjunction with its right adjoint identified by the specified scalar-change isomorphism.
